title.narrative: Strengthening of advocacy processes on environmental issues in El Salvador.

description.narrative: El Salvador has 590 rivers, 70% of which are polluted (Bishops' Conference, 2021). The Salvadoran state has historically refused to recognise the human right to water at the constitutional level. This has had an impact in terms of low public investment in the most vulnerable communities, as well as increased local and national conflicts with companies that, in the absence of legal protection, use water for commercial purposes without appropriate regulation. This is aggravated by the fact that, due to its geographical location, the country's original water sources come from transboundary basins between Honduras and Guatemala, which means that any extractive activity in those countries puts El Salvador's water availability in greater crisis. There are also clear signs that the current government intends to repeal the Law banning metallic mining (passed in 2017), such as political openness with investors in this industry, the promotion of alliances for "responsible mining for sustainable development", as well as the creation of public entities with competences related to mining, without distinguishing its type and scope. The project aims to raise awareness at social, church, and institutional levels about the consequences of 3 specific business initiatives with regional, national, and local impact in the areas of mining and construction that threaten El Salvador's water sustainability, increase forced displacement, and produce legal uncertainty. The aim is to contribute to stop the progress of their implementation by developing strategies that strengthen community organisation processes, social dialogue, legal defence, and environmental protection mechanisms in an integrated manner. The partnership will also work to deepen intersectoral alliances to promote legal instruments against transboundary mining. In addition, systematic work will be developed to dignify the role of environmental defenders and strengthen community water management.
